findings.summary: The ordinary author page owns a duplicated author-profile loading and stale-response state machine.
findings.consequence: Future fixes to profile request identity, handoff cleanup, canonical-path rejection, SSR status mapping, or client stale-response behavior must be applied in both this route and the Dramawebben sibling route, increasing drift risk in a route already flagged for SSR state.
findings.evidence: Line 52 starts the page-local useAsyncData loader; app/pages/författare/[author]/dramawebben.vue has the same ProfileResponse shape, route validation, authorId/asyncKey/currentIdentity/pendingIdentity guards, profileHandoffs useState key, API GET to /authors/{author_id}, safeAuthorCanonicalPath rejection, and status mapping. The first route-specific policy inside this loader is only the ordinary-vs-dramawebben view selection around lines 75-80.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared loader, identity guard, handoff lookup/cleanup, and status mapping into a small author-profile route composable parameterized by variant and canonical redirect policy; keep this page responsible only for ordinary metadata/background/template rendering and ordinary-specific canonical handling.
